title: Tokenizer shim + chat-template synchronization for model import
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem summary:
Imported model variants arrive with different tokenizer encodings (SentencePiece vs BPE vs cl100k), and some community chat templates use model-specific special-token markers. During onboarding this causes: 1) inaccurate token counts in performance profiles, 2) chat-template mismatches (system/message separators tokenized differently) that break streaming prefix caching, and 3) occasional off-by-one length errors for truncation.

Goal:
Create a compatibility shim and validation pipeline that normalizes tokenizer outputs at import time, keeps a model-version pin for the tokenizer mapping, and ensures chat templates are synchronized with the model's canonical tokenization before publishing the model's performance profile. The pipeline must be auditable and reversible for rollback.

Background & motivation:
- Performance profiles published to the model catalog are used by routing and batching heuristics; incorrect tokenization skews latency/cost estimates.
- Customers pin model versions; if onboarded tokenizers drift between imports, pinned versions must preserve the tokenizer mapping.
- Console and SDK expect chat templates standardized (e.g. system delimiters) so runtime batching and KV-caching can rely on prefix invariants.

Non-goals:
- Replacing a model's native tokenizer nor forcing users to re-train. This is purely an onboarding compatibility layer and validation step.

Design decisions so far:
1) Tokenizer shim: implement a lightweight adapter that maps special tokens and token boundaries into a small canonical space during onboarding (not at runtime inference). The shim outputs a mapping table (original_token -> canonical_token_id) and a tokenization-diff artifact.
2) Chat-template linter: static checks run during import to verify system/message separators map to expected canonical tokens. If mismatched, the import is flagged and a suggestion patch is generated.
3) Version pinning: store the tokenizer-hash and mapping in the model registry entry (model_manifest.tokenizer_hash). Any subsequent imports of same model version must match hash or go through a forced compatibility review.
4) Perf profile publishing gated: performance profile job will not publish until tokenization-validation passes. If it fails, a draft profile is stored and QA is notified.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenizer+Compatibility+Shim
- RFC (notes): https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-02-tokenizer-shim.md
- Import CI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234
- Perf profile test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-tools/pull/67

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarding pipeline produces a tokenization-diff artifact for every imported model and fails import if chat-template linter detects critical mismatches.
- model_manifest includes tokenizer_hash and mapping_url fields for all new entries.
- Performance profile jobs are blocked from publishing when tokenization validation fails; a draft profile is retained and linked.
- Automated tests covering: emoji tokenization, long system-prefixes (4k chars), and mixed-script inputs.
- Manual QA checklist completed by Console and Runtime owners and signoff from Product.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives: linter may flag acceptable token differences. Mitigation: add a tolerances table and a human-in-the-loop override path with auditor logging.
- Storage overhead for mapping artifacts: store compressed diffs and enforce TTL for draft artifacts.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge import CI and shim behind feature flag import.tokenizer_shim (PR 1234).
2) Run on internal models and run full perf-harness for 2 weeks in dry-run mode (no publish).
3) Enable canary auto-publish for a small set of trusted OSS models.
4) Full rollout once metrics indicate <0.1% false-positive rate and no customer-reported regressions.

Backout plan:
- Disable import.tokenizer_shim feature flag and revert PR 1234. Old model manifests remain unchanged; cached performance profiles continue to be served.

QA & test plan:
- Unit tests for mapping generator and chat-template linter (coverage target 90%).
- Integration test: import 20 community models covering cl100k, bpe and sentencepiece; compare canonical token counts against ground truth.
- Fuzz test for uncommon unicode sequences (emojis, ZWJ sequences).
- E2E smoke: ensure streaming always retains prefix size estimates used by router.

Notes on implementation details:
- Use existing tokenization library wrappers (tokenizers v0.14) and add an adapter layer in onboarding-api.
- Mapping format: newline-separated rows of "orig_token_hex -> canonical_id" compressed with gzip. Mapping stored in S3 with lifecycle 180 days for drafts.
- Add metric: onboarding.tokenizer_mismatch{severity} with tags model_id, import_id to track frequency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) tokenization-diff artifact emitted for every import; 2) model_manifest.tokenizer_hash present and immutable for a given model version; 3) perf profile publish blocked when validation fails; 4) QA signoff recorded in import audit log.
steps: 1) Implement adapter + mapping generator in onboarding-api (owner: Rohan). 2) Implement chat-template linter and auto-suggest patch generator (owner: Mei Chen). 3) Wire validation gate into perf publishing job (owner: Samir Rao). 4) Add telemetry and alerts (owner: InfraOps). 5) Run dry-run on internal bucket -> collect metrics -> iterate. 6) Canary and full rollout.

notes: Edge-case found during spike: some community templates use invisible separator U+2063. Linter will normalize those to canonical <sep> token and log suggestion. Also added test vectors for ZWNJ/ZWJ sequences.
